voyage.name: Zagreb Cathedral
voyage.hours: It is closed due to March 2020 earthquake damage
voyage.content: The Zagreb Cathedral with its twin spires is the most well known landmark of the city. The original cathedral dates back to 1217 but the present structure dates to 1906. The chief architect was Hermann Bollé.

voyage.name: St. Mark's Square
voyage.content: St. Mark's Church is known for its colourful roof tiles depicting the coat of arms of Croatia and Zagreb. St. Mark's Church was constructed in 1499.

voyage.name: St. Catherine's Church
voyage.content: Baroque style church

voyage.name: Old Town Gate
voyage.address: at the top of Radićeva street
voyage.content: now a shrine to virgin Mary - the "Kamenita vrata" where you can light a candle and, as the locals believe, your wish will be granted. Please be silent, even if just passing through the Gate. The portrait of Mary is said to be sacred, because it is the only thing that survived the large fire. Near the Old Town Gate is the sculpture of St. George having slain the dragon. The other statue, him fighting the dragon, is l

voyage.name: Ribnjak Park
voyage.content: the Ribnjak is an English-style park complete with exotic plants, sculptures, and a children's playground. The park used to be the site of Bishop's fish pond.

voyage.name: Museum of Broken Relationships
voyage.content: What remains after a break-up? Museum's permanent display is an opportunity to experience a unique emotional journey through dozens of love leftovers collected from all around the world. Museum is also the winner of Kenneth Hudson Award 2011 for the most innovative museum in Europe.

voyage.name: Museum of Hangovers
voyage.content: Specialty museum about nightlife culture and hangovers; interactive exhibits and short visit (45–60 min).

voyage.name: Klovićevi Dvori Gallery
voyage.content: This gallery in the old Jesuit monastery with changing exhibitions introduces Croatian and foreign cultural and artistic heritage across all eras. In most exhibitions, photography without flash is permitted.

voyage.name: Zagreb City Museum
voyage.content: The permanent collection tells the history of the city but there are also temporary exhibitions

voyage.name: Lotrščak Tower
voyage.content: Great local views if you are prepared to climb the spiral staircase.

voyage.name: Grič Tunnel
voyage.content: A 450-m-long pedestrian tunnel that was built as bomb shelter is sometimes used for concerts.

voyage.name: Sabor Palace
voyage.content: The seat of the Croatian Parliament.

voyage.name: Ban's Palace
voyage.content: The former home of the viceroys of Croatia, which is now used by the government.

voyage.name: Strossmayer Square
voyage.content: Named after Josip Juraj Strossmayer, politician and Roman Catholic Bishop.

voyage.name: Zrinjevac Square
voyage.content: The park of the Academy, connecting the Zrinjevac and Tomislav parks.

voyage.name: King Tomislav Square
voyage.content: Decorated with floor beds and fountains and lined with trees it is dominated by a horse mounted statue of King Tomislav.

voyage.name: Botanical Gardens
voyage.price: Regular €2, students and pupils €1, children free
voyage.content: Arboretum, greenhouses, Croatian flora, rock gardens, annuals, perennials, and a few animals.

voyage.name: Mažuranić Square
voyage.content: Named after Croatian poet Ivan Mažuranić.

voyage.name: Marulić Square
voyage.content: Marulić Square houses the Croatia State Archive, and a statue of Marko Marulić.

voyage.name: Republic of Croatia Square
voyage.content: One of the largest and greenest squares of Zagreb, with the Croatian National Theatre in its centre.

voyage.name: Mimara Museum
voyage.hours: Closed to public since the March 2020 earthquake
voyage.content: Houses some 3,700 works of art donated by Ante Topić Mimara. The collection comprises more than 1,500 exhibits dating from the prehistoric period up to the 20th century. Some of the most famous exhibits include works by Lorenzetti, Raffaello, Giorgione, Veronese, Caravaggio, Canaletto, 60 paintings by the Dutch masters Rembrandt, Van Goyen, Ruisdael, 50 works by the Flemish masters Van der Weyden, Bosch, Rubens, Van

voyage.name: Archaeological Museum
voyage.hours: Opening hours have been limited since the 2020 earthquake; check the website
voyage.content: Possesses over 400,000 objects, not all of them being exhibited. The holdings include evidence of Croatian presence in this area as well as rare samples which have made the museum known to the whole world. The most famous are the Egyptian collection, the Zagreb mummy and bandages with the oldest Etruscan inscription in the world (Liber Linteus Zagrabiensis), and the numismatic collection. A part of the museum is set

voyage.name: Art Pavilion in Zagreb
voyage.content: Designed by the Hungarian architects Korb and Giergl for the Millennium Exhibition 1896 in Budepest, its iron frame was transported to Zagreb after the exhibition, where the permanent pavillion was built by the famous Viennese designers of theatres in Central Europe Hellmer and Fellmer. It is a neo-classical exhibition complex and one of the landmarks of the city centre. The exhibitions are also held in the impressiv

voyage.name: Croatian National Theatre
voyage.content: Croatian National Theatre, Zagreb was built in 1895. There are also Croatian National Theatres in Split, Rijeka, Osijek, Varaždin and Zadar.

voyage.name: Modern Gallery
voyage.content: Exhibits fine artists of the 19th and 20th centuries.

voyage.name: National Museum of Modern Art
voyage.content: Closed for renovation.

voyage.name: Josip Račić Gallery
voyage.content: Second smaller site of the National Museum of Modern art hosting temporary exhibitions.

voyage.name: People and Art House Lauba
voyage.alt: Kuća za ljude i umjetnost Lauba
voyage.content: Presents works from the Filip Trade Collection, a large private collection of modern and contemporary Croatian art and current artistic production.

voyage.name: Museum of Arts and Crafts
voyage.content: Closed for reconstruction

voyage.name: Technical Museum Nikola Tesla
voyage.price: Adult €4, under 7 free, senior and student €3
voyage.content: Has a lot of technical inventions, fire engines, a cabinet of Nikola Tesla, a planetarium and an underground mine.

voyage.name: Museum of Illusions
voyage.content: Prepare to be deceived. A few exhibits are more suited to two people.

voyage.name: Typhlological Museum
voyage.price: Adults €3; students & schoolchildren €2; disabled & pensioners free
voyage.content: Rather specialised museum focusing on the history of institutions for the blind, writing systems for the blind and other visual impairments together with more modern developments. There is a dark room where you can experience what it is like not to see and identify objects in the dark.

voyage.name: The Grounded Sun
voyage.content: Prizemljeno sunce by Ivan Kožarić is a 1971 sculpture, a 2-m-wide bronze sphere, which represents the scale model of the Sun, with 9 planets of the solar system in their scaled size compared to this Sun. Mercury is in Margaretska street, a couple of hundred meters to the west, turn right after reaching Cvjetni trg, you should see it on the wall to the right after passing a dozen or so meters. Venus is on the pole of

voyage.name: Maksimir Park & Zagreb Zoo
voyage.content: The biggest park in Zagreb. Great place to chill out, drink coffee, eat lunch (picnic or at the park's restaurant) or take nice long walks through the forest or by the small lakes. Good for joggers, cyclists, also child and dog friendly. Offers lake rowing. The zoo has red pandas. It has operated since the 1930s.

voyage.name: Mirogoj Cemetery
voyage.content: Mirogoj is the central cemetery of Zagreb. It was opened in 1876 north of the city centre. The mortuary, the impressive and picturesque arcades with the church of Christ the King (architect H. Bollé, 1883-1914) make it one of the most impressive cemeteries in the world. Here stand the tombs of notable personalities (including that of basketball hero Drazen Petrovic) who are relevant to Croatian history. To arrive fro

voyage.name: Medvedgrad Castle and Medvednica
voyage.price: Visitor Centre Adults €7.95 (weekends), €6.6 (weekday) many other ticket options
voyage.content: The imposing mountain overlooking Zagreb (Medvednica) contains a preserved fortress (Medvedgrad) and fascinating views of the city. Being respectful in the fort is a good idea, since it is the site of the Altar of the Homeland memorial, dedicated to Croatian soldiers who died in the Homeland war. There are several historical festivals during the year, including knights tournaments.

voyage.name: Jarun
voyage.content: Jarun Lake is a recreational area based around a large lake where locals go to relax, exercise - and party! The centrepiece of the area is the lake, which is used for windsurfing and has a large rowing section with spectator stands. There are also shingle beaches surrounding the water, alongside which are several bars that get very busy during the weekends but are also nice for a sunny lunchtime snack. All the bars t

voyage.name: Bundek
voyage.content: Park with lake, hosts horticultural shows, firework festivals, workshops, concerts and music festivals (mostly during the summer).

voyage.name: Museum of Contemporary Art
voyage.price: From about €4, scroll down visitor information page on website to see all prices; first Wednesday free
voyage.content: Follows and presents contemporary trends in fine arts.

voyage.name: Croatian Museum of Naïve Art
voyage.content: Houses more than one thousand works belonging to Croatian naïve art.

voyage.name: Strossmayerovo šetalište
voyage.content: In the summer, it is an outdoor scene for painters, musicians and other artists offering food, drinks, performances and concerts. Popular meeting place for all ages, with a great view of the Lower Town.

voyage.name: Snow Queen Trophy
voyage.content: Ladies Night Slalom : Zagreb is the only capital in the world that hosts a Ski World Cup race. The slalom event - known as the "Snow Queen Trophy" (Snježna kraljica) - usually takes place in January. It is the most expensive race on the women's world cup tour and an exceptionally popular sporting event in Croatia that attracts a crowd of around 25 thousand people.

voyage.name: Cineplexx Centar Kaptol
voyage.content: A multiplex cinema (5 screens) within the Kaptol Shopping Centre north of the Cathedral.

voyage.name: Cineplexx City Centre One East
voyage.content: A multiplex cinema (7 screens) on the east side of Zagreb.

voyage.name: Kino Tuškanac
voyage.price: Entrance for programs Kinoteka and Restauracije is free, regular ticket is €4
voyage.content: Showing much more than just European filmography, alternative and older films. Films are screened in their original language with only Croatian subtites.

voyage.name: Turistički Informativni Centar
voyage.content: Sells everything ranging from postcards and books to pottery and crystal

voyage.name: GEA Gallery
voyage.content: a wide range of souvenirs that are handmade in Croatia and are very reasonably priced. Very knowledgeable staff.

voyage.name: Millennium
voyage.content: Pottery, crystal, costume jewellery, and other gifts.

voyage.name: Nocturno
voyage.content: Good place to try the local gastronomy. An excellent restaurant with a variety of offers and helpful staff and a pleasant atmosphere.

voyage.name: Sandwich Bar Pingvin
voyage.content: Classic sandwich bar with a wide menu and reasonably good mix of languages. One of the most popular dishes is the toplo/hladno (hot/cold), a grilled chicken and vegetables sandwich.

voyage.name: La Štruk
voyage.content: One of Zagreb's oldest fast food spots. Highly recommended are the grilled cheese sandwich, the grilled stuffed lungic and the zagrebacki sandwich.

voyage.name: Taquitos Bandidos
voyage.content: Exactly what street food should be. Simple, fast, tasty and well thought out creative dishes that surprise you and overdeliver. Try their amazing chipotle sauce! It's Mexican street food.

voyage.name: Plac Kitchen & Grill
voyage.content: Tasty Cevapcici sausages, fast service and not expensive. Fantastic peppers, cevapi and great special burgers. The restaurant is a bit hidden.

voyage.name: Bistro Dolac
voyage.content: Somewhat of a Zagreb institution. The decoration is very "old school" (high ceilings, pot plants, yellow walls, functional furniture).

voyage.name: Amfora
voyage.content: Seafood Restaurant

voyage.name: MS Grill Restaurant
voyage.content: It's a family owned local restaurant. The staff is very nice and welcoming

voyage.name: Restaurant Kvatric
voyage.content: Croatian restaurant with very nice food for a reasonable price. Has a nice terrance in the back garden. Close to tramstop 'Kvaternikov Trg'.

voyage.name: Mali Medo
voyage.content: Another traditional Croatian restaurant. Lively atmosphere, youthful clientele, and all very affordable. Excellent ćevapčići and gulaš, not to mention superb beer.

voyage.name: Zrno bio bistro
voyage.content: Almost all vegan and organic. Some ingredients come from their own Zrno farm, less than an hour away. Mains rich in umami, luscious desserts. An extensive beer and wine list.

voyage.name: VegeHop
voyage.content: Vegan dishes.

voyage.name: Koykan Gajeva
voyage.content: Italian piadinas, Japanese teriyaki sticks, oriental wraps, Bubble tea from Taiwan and Japanese mochi cakes.

voyage.name: Oliva
voyage.content: Italian restaurant (pizza, pasta).

voyage.name: Stara Sava
voyage.content: An excellent pizzeria.

voyage.name: Food Garden
voyage.content: Healthy Eating restaurant mainly plant based with some pescetarian options.

voyage.name: Boban
voyage.content: Italian food.

voyage.name: Le Bistro
voyage.content: A French restaurant within the Regent Esplanade Hotel.

voyage.name: Restaurant Suhina
voyage.content: An old family-run restaurant on the old Samobor road that offers a variety of roasted food.

voyage.name: Takenoko
voyage.address: Nova Ves 11, in Kaptol Centar Shopping Centre
voyage.content: Zagreb may not be synonymous with sushi restaurants, but this one is superb. It is not cheap, but the sushi they make is incredible.

voyage.name: Velika Klet Obitelji Bunčić
voyage.content: A very popular place that offers Croatian cuisine, live music on weekends, a stable, fish pond and basketball courtyard.

voyage.name: 100% juice bar
voyage.content: Pricey but a good place to get a healthy snack or fruit smoothie.

voyage.name: SladoMazo
voyage.content: A pancake restaurant with a wide range of crazy both sweet and salty filling ideas.

voyage.name: The Cookie Factory
voyage.content: Homebaked American sweets. Cookies, brownies and bars, krispy treats, muffins, cupcakes, banana breads, scones, cobblers, biscotti, top notch coffee, smoothies, cakes and pies.

voyage.name: Torte i To
voyage.address: Nova Ves 11, second floor of the Kaptol Centar
voyage.content: A great little caffe offering the best cheese cake in town, and other great cakes.

voyage.name: Vincek
voyage.content: The local, best-known ice cream and cake palace in town centre. Offers diet foods.

voyage.name: Konoba Didov San
voyage.content: Excellent food, unique menu, large portions and great location.

voyage.name: Booksa
voyage.content: A cafe, bookshop and library famous with local young intellectuals.

voyage.name: Cica
voyage.content: Bar mostly known for its great and varied choice of the local schnappses (rakija). Interesting always changing, gallery-like interior. The whole bar is small but offers outdoor seating. Very popular and crowded, brimming with young business and student clientele.

voyage.name: Funk club
voyage.content: Cafe and bar that offers various music night programmes in the basement (mostly alternative, DJs, world music) and spacial backpacker evenings. Very good atmosphere, lots of character, cheap and tasty Rakija shoots and excellent electronic music: funky, electro, jazz, d'n'b, house, dubstep.

voyage.name: Golf
voyage.content: Popular golf-themed cafe/bar.

voyage.name: KIC
voyage.content: Offers free internet and cheap international call centre. Hosts a cinema with various alternative movies.

voyage.name: Kino Grič
voyage.content: Old cinema. Hosts movies, festivals, music nights and Zagreb's hipster crowd.

voyage.name: Mali Medo
voyage.content: Offers a good choice of local beer and food. Indoors smoking prohibited. Has a terrace facing Tkalčićeva street.

voyage.name: Melin
voyage.content: A cheap bar brimming with young people and students. Offers indoors, a roofed terraced leveled seating and an open terrace facing Tkalčićeva street. Known for crowds of people often drinking even around the bar, in the park and playground in front of it.

voyage.name: Oliver Twist
voyage.content: A choice of good Irish beer with a great atmosphere. Big summer terrace in front.

voyage.name: Portal
voyage.content: Next to Melin, offers same service, the Portal and Melin crowds often mix at the outdoors terraces.

voyage.name: Purgeraj
voyage.content: A bar/club in the Ribnjak park in the city centre. Offers mostly rock, blues and alternative music. Daily happy hour when you get two drinks for the price of one. Sometimes hosts concerts. Popular with student crowd esp on Thursdays when it hosts the popular "take me out" evening offering a mix of indie and alternative music. In the summer, outside Purgeraj, in the Ribnjak park there are live concerts and various wor

voyage.name: Tolkien's House
voyage.content: A small fantasy cafe/bar for Tolkien lovers. Offers a variety of beers, cider and hot drinks.

voyage.name: ŽeraBar
voyage.content: Bar owned by Crvena jabuka frontman Dražen Žerić.

voyage.name: Garden Brewery Taproom
voyage.content: Out of town brewery tap. Two food concessions on-site. 12+ craft beers brewed on-site.

voyage.name: Aquarius
voyage.content: Saturday night is drum'n'bass & dancehall music, Friday is hip-hop/r'n'b night. Good concerts.

voyage.name: BP Club
voyage.content: Jazz and blues lovers should check it out.

voyage.name: Funk club
voyage.content: Very good atmosphere, lots of character, cheap and tasty Rakija shoots and excellent electronic music: funky, electro, jazz, d'n'b, house, dubstep!

voyage.name: Jabuka
voyage.content: Cult club for alternative, punk music. Cheap drinks opened on weekends, often concerts of alternative bands. Mostly visited on weekends, especially Fridays. Admission fee: €3.5.

voyage.name: KSET
voyage.price: Entrance prices from €1.5 (students) to €6-8 for concerts
voyage.content: A popular student club. Offers various indie and alternative programmes every night of the week. Indoors smoking prohibited. Serves only beer and non alcoholic drinks.

voyage.name: Medika
voyage.content: A local alternative club/legalized squat usually loaded with people during weekends, playing various music genres until the early morning. Best Croatian beers for €1.5.

voyage.name: Močvara
voyage.content: A local alternative club (rock, punk, metal, indie) with various concerts and theme nights/programmes. Sometimes hosts festivals, young indie talent concerts, movie nights, exhibitions.

voyage.name: SAX! - Klub hrvatskih glazbenika
voyage.content: A great place to enjoy live music of a wide array of styles including blues, jazz, rock and pop.

voyage.name: The Jazz Club
voyage.content: Jazz, blues, and funk bands, often from other countries.

voyage.name: Whole Wide World Hostel
voyage.content: Lively backpacker hostel with a bar

voyage.name: Chillout Hostel Zagreb
voyage.content: A hostel in the city centre, free linen, free towels, free wifi, 24-hr bar and reception

voyage.name: Fulir Hostel Zagreb
voyage.content: 2 rooms, including a 12-bed dorm. Great place to meet people, but can be a wait to use the bathroom.

voyage.name: Hobo Bear Hostel
voyage.content: A cozy hostel very near the town centre. There is a basement hang out lounge with a TV, including cable and many DVDs, as well as free (fast) internet and computers. The staff is amazingly helpful and speak perfect English, the beds are comfortable and come with free linens and blankets, and there is also a well stocked kitchen facility.

voyage.name: Hostel Lika
voyage.content: Small and cozy hostel a bit out of the city centre.

voyage.name: Nokturno Hostel
voyage.content: Free internet access, free linens and towels.

voyage.name: Logistics Youth Centre
voyage.content: Logistic youth centre, also works as a regional information centre. From the host, you can get complete information about everything that interests you. The space has 10 rooms, lobby with fireplace, dining room, kitchen and a cinema hall, where you can stream movies from your laptop. The most interesting part is the terrace with space for tents and 30 seats. Located further from downtown, but the centre has its own b

voyage.name: HI Hostel Zagreb
voyage.content: Convenient for main station. HI Hostel but can also be booked on common booking sites.

voyage.name: Hotel Jägerhorn
voyage.content: 3-star hotel founded in 1827, Hotel Jägerhorn is the city's oldest standing hotel.

voyage.name: Arcotel Allegra
voyage.content: 4-star hotel which is Zagreb's first "lifestyle" hotel. All rooms are spacious and air-conditioned and feature mini bar, safe, internet connection, bigscreen TV and DVD player. A very cool touch are the free apples supplied in your room in a very funky holder!

voyage.name: Best Western Premier Hotel Astoria
voyage.content: 3-star hotel

voyage.name: Panorama Hotel Zagreb
voyage.content: 4-star hotel.

voyage.name: Hotel Aristos
voyage.content: 4-star hotel.

voyage.name: Hotel As
voyage.content: 4-star hotel.

voyage.name: Hotel Central
voyage.content: 66 room, 3-star hotel.

voyage.name: Hotel Dubrovnik
voyage.content: 4-star hotel. Clean, centrally located, good service. Some rooms are small.

voyage.name: Hotel I
voyage.content: 3-star hotel.

voyage.name: Hotel International
voyage.content: 3-star hotel.

voyage.name: Hotel Jadran
voyage.content: 3-star hotel. There is a big shopping centre near-by - the Importanne Gallery.

voyage.name: Hotel Laguna
voyage.content: 3-star hotel.

voyage.name: Hotel Phoenix
voyage.content: 3-star hotel

voyage.name: Palace Hotel
voyage.content: 4-star hotel. It was built in the Secession style in 1891 and converted into a hotel in 1905. The Arts Pavilion is 50 m away.

voyage.name: Esplanade Zagreb
voyage.content: Built in 1925 for passengers of the famous Orient Express train, which connected Paris and Istanbul. If you can, check the Emerald Ballroom with its soaring dome shaped roof. The hotel includes the Zinfandel's Restaurant, Le Bistro and the Esplanade 1925, the hotel's lounge and cocktail bar.

voyage.name: Sheraton Zagreb Hotel
voyage.content: Features air-conditioned rooms and suites with classic furniture and marbled bathrooms. It also includes King Tomislav Restaurant, Fontana Restaurant, Piano Bar, Café Imperial, 17 meeting rooms and an 800-m² Grand Ballroom.

voyage.name: Westin Zagreb
voyage.content: The hotel features the Heavenly Bed and Heavenly Shower and probably offers the best view in the city.

voyage.name: Boutique hotel Le Premier Zagreb
voyage.content: 5-star hotel
